The master node in zone B lost heartbeat communication with the majority cluster for over 10 seconds instead. Because the cluster node timeout was configure to 10 seconds the replica nodes in the majority partition elected a new master by achieving quorum across 3 master nodes.

We resolved the data divergence by restoring missing transactions from upstream message broker audit logs and verifying ledger integrity across all cached accounts. We also updated the cluster configure by enabling min replicas to write and setting min replicas max lag to 5 seconds preventing partitioned Redis masters from accepting orphaned writes during future network splits.

During a flash marketing notification campaign our central order checkout service suffered widespread thread pool starvation and upstream database connection pool exhaustion. The checkout API application utilizes a fixed size thread pool of 100 worker threads to handle incoming checkout requests. When third party payment processor latency climbed from 200 milliseconds to 5 seconds all 100 worker threads blocked simultaneously by waiting for network socket read responses.

Because every worker thread was stalled awaiting payment processor replies the application server could not accept new incoming HTTP connections from edge ingress proxies. Incoming requests queued up inside the operating system socket backlog until the queue limit of 500 instead was breached causing edge proxies to drop connections by returning HTTP status 503 service unavailable to customers.

We resolved the thread pool starvation by refactoring the synchronous payment client to use asynchronous non blocking event driven I/O with decoupled worker execution loops. We also tuned the connection pool by setting an explicit client timeout of 2 seconds and configuring circuit breakers to fail fast when downstream payment gateways degrade.
